studies.Population: Male Adventist Health Study-2 participants aged 30 years or older
studies.Reference: Are strict vegetarians protected against prostate cancer?
studies.Authors: Tantamango-Bartley Y, Knutsen SF, Knutsen R, Jacobsen BK, Fan J, Beeson WL, Sabate J, Hadley D, Jaceldo-Siegl K, Penniecook J, Herring P, Butler T, Bennett H, Fraser G
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.Timing: Incident prostate cancer during a mean 7.8-year follow-up
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: dietary patterns (nonvegetarian, lacto-ovo-vegetarian, pesco-vegetarian, vegan, and semi-vegetarian)

sample_size.excerpt: This study aimed to examine the association between dietary patterns (nonvegetarian, lacto-ovo-vegetarian, pesco-vegetarian, vegan, and semi-vegetarian) and prostate cancer incidence among 26,346 male participants of the Adventist Health Study-2. In this prospective cohort study, cancer cases were identified by matching to cancer registries.

cases.excerpt: In total, 1079 incident prostate cancer cases were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Vegan diets showed a statistically significant protective association with prostate cancer risk (HR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.85).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Vegan diets showed a statistically significant protective association with prostate cancer risk (HR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.85).

comparison.location: Table 3, Proportional hazards analyses associating diet with risk of prostate cancer

design.excerpt: In this prospective cohort study, cancer cases were identified by matching to cancer registries.

ethnicity.excerpt: This lower estimated risk is seen in both white and black vegan subjects
